projects.title: ANF System
projects.subtitle: Adoración Nocturna Filipina National Council
projects.paragraph: I started it while working as the Council's assistant office manager, to automate the paperwork I was handling. It covers the Council's stock, Official Receipts, cash and check vouchers, petty cash, members, annual dues and officers, and runs on a single office PC. Officers can reach it from their phones over the office WiFi, and nothing goes to the cloud. Every peso and centavo is exact, and a checked backup is made within about two minutes of any change. Built test-first, with every screen checked at nine widths in two browser engines, 1,000+ layout checks in all. It has been in use since September 2026, and I'm adding online ordering. The 4,000+ is 4,170 checks, all passing, on Sep 12, 2026, and the layout checks were 1,092 at the release of Sep 24, 2026; both have grown since. The documentation counts the screens two ways, so I round down to 20+.

projects.title: EyeDTrack
projects.subtitle: Driver attention monitoring, thesis and solo rebuild
projects.paragraph: I led our thesis team in 2025, and a teammate updated the app in mid-2026. From October 2026 I rebuilt it alone, directing an AI coding agent, and measured it. A Kotlin app on an Android phone sends camera frames over the driver's own network to a Python and Flask server, which finds the face with dlib's 68 facial landmarks and OpenCV and measures how open the eyes and mouth are and where the head points. A time rule decides what counts, the app speaks the alert, and when it can't see the face it says so instead of guessing. I tested it once on people it had never seen: it met 0 of its 15 accuracy targets, and the project site says so. The 713 ms is the 95th percentile from camera capture to result, on one phone at a desk on Nov 11, 2026; it rose to 887 ms with the server PC heavily loaded. The 26 of 30 is an idealized episode count from that sealed final test, and the same count missed 22 yawn episodes. It's an academic prototype, not a safety device.
